messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High latency signature detected on pool-shared-gpu-3. p95 > 1.2s, p99 > 6s, streaming stalls increased. Paging oncall @Anna (oncall)
Anna (oncall): ack, I'm looking. pulling up dashboards now
Anna (oncall): p95 jumped from 160ms -> 1.25s around 13:08 UTC, p99 ~6.2s. Request rate steady. Streaming stalls: 0.8% -> 7.6%
Lee (runtime): seeing heavy writeback and IO wait on host gpu-hw-47. KV cache evictions spiked. suspect noisy tenant in pool-shared-gpu-3
Raj (infra): checking host-level telemetry. iostat shows high md throughput, cgroup blkio throttling events.
Raj (infra): quick logs:
```
[13:09:21] blkio: cgroup writeback burst, tasks=1, write_kb=120000
[13:09:22] nvlink: pci-bus 0000:65:00: blk_mq queue depth spike
```
Jordan (eng-sre): which tenant(s) on that host? need to identify top IO processes
Anna (oncall): listing containers on gpu-hw-47 ->
```
$ ssh gpu-hw-47 sudo crictl ps --labels pool=shared-gpu-3
CONTAINER   PID   IMAGE                OWNER
c-89a       3456  redwood/runtime:3   tenant:acme-ml
c-92f       4120  redwood/runtime:3   tenant:edge-sent
c-7d3       4890  redwood/worker:2    tenant:research-beta
```
Anna (oncall): acme-ml showing heavy disk write and long-running checkpointing job
Sam (product): Mei, any active customer reports? Could be impacting some SLAs
Mei (customer-success): Acme reported intermittent streaming stalls in their production app. Opening support ticket now. Customer-facing note ready if needed.
Olivia (ops): short-term mitigation: can we throttle/checkpoint frequency for the acme tenant? We can also migrate it off this host.
Lee (runtime): We can force-evict the tenant's pods to another host in same pool (prefer cold migration to avoid data loss). Migration command:
```
# cordon host
kubectl cordon gpu-hw-47
# evict tenant pods
kubectl delete pod -l tenant=acme-ml -n runtime --grace-period=30
```
Raj (infra): we have spare capacity in pool-shared-gpu-5 and pool-dedicated-1 (burst). Recommend migrating to pool-shared-gpu-5 first.
Jordan (eng-sre): before evicting, reduce cgroup writeback limit to buy time:
```
echo 1048576 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/gpu-hw-47/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```
Jordan (eng-sre): doing that now
Anna (oncall): cgroup write limit applied. IO rates dropping a bit. p95 improving to ~560ms
Olivia (ops): initiate live migration to pool-shared-gpu-5, moving only acme tenants
Lee (runtime): kicking eviction for tenant acme-ml now
deploy-bot: evict request accepted for pods [c-89a]. Reschedule to nodes: [gpu-hw-81,gpu-hw-83]
Anna (oncall): pods rescheduled; acme pod restarted on gpu-hw-81
Anna (oncall): p95 down to 210ms, p99 ~480ms, streaming stalls back to 1.2%
Mei (customer-success): informed Acme: "We routed your workloads away from impacted host; you may see transient reconnects. We are monitoring." Customer response: "Thanks, reduction noticed but still occasional hiccups"
Sam (product): should consider offering them temporary dedicated capacity if their checkpoint workload is heavy
Raj (infra): follow-up: root cause seems to be periodic heavy checkpointing causing sustained write bursts; cgroup blkio default burst allowed it to saturate host NVMe write queue
Jordan (eng-sre): suggested medium-term mitigations:
- enforce per-tenant background IO QoS
- throttle checkpointing via runtime config for large models
- add proactive eviction policy when write_bps > X for > Y seconds
Lee (runtime): posting a small patch to runtime to detect high kv-cache-evict IO and downgrade background checkpointing frequency
```
diff --git a/runtime/io_control.py b/runtime/io_control.py
index 123..abc 100644
+ if write_bps > THRESHOLD:
+     reduce_checkpoint_freq()
```
Anna (oncall): scheduled follow-up: rotate the noisy tenant to dedicated capacity in 2 hours unless their job completes
Mei (customer-success): offered dedicated trial, Acme requested brief window to test. I've created GA ticket and CC'd account team
Olivia (ops): re-enabled original cgroup limits to normal now that load migrated
Jordan (eng-sre): will run host-level fio to validate sustained throughput after mitigation
Raj (infra): ran quick fio baseline on gpu-hw-47, results show write latency back to normal
```
$ fio --name=writebw --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --rw=write --bs=1m --size=1G --iodepth=16
writebw: bw=800MB/s, lat=1.9ms
```
Anna (oncall): closing alert if metrics stable for 15m. Current window: p95 180ms, p99 420ms, stalls 0.9%
Sam (product): add to RCA backlog: tenant-level IO QoS, improved observability for cgroup writeback, customer-facing postmortem if Acme impacted production significantly
Mei (customer-success): confirming customer is happy with mitigation for now. Will escalate if they still see <SLA degradation>
Anna (oncall): marking incident resolved but keeping thread open for RCA notes. Thanks all :heart:
Jordan (eng-sre): opened GH issue redwood/runtime#4287 for checkpoint throttling and eviction policy
Lee (runtime): linking PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1287
Anna (oncall): final note: recommend runbook update: "noisy-io-tenant" and add automated migration play
Olivia (ops): copied runbook changes to /docs/incidents/noisy-io.md
Anna (oncall): last check-in at 13:35 UTC, closing thread
